 Why DSP Multi Asset Omni FoF is increasing gold and silver allocation amid 2026 price crash
 By Ayush Khar 4 min read | Updated on November 20, 2026, 18:20 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 The mutual fund house added that while peer funds remained neutral or overweight on precious metals, the DSP scheme ran a 50% underweight position on gold and silver.
 The change in strategy is anchored in DSP's five-point valuation and macroeconomic framework for precious metals. Representational image/Shutterstock
 Globally gold and silver prices have retreated significantly from the record highs they touched earlier in 2026. The effect of this decline is visible in the price of physical gold and silver and in commodity futures as well. Amid this decline, DSP Mutual Fund has announced that it is changing its investment strategy for its scheme DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds (FoF).

 As gold and silver prices decline, the fund house is changing its long-held underweight stance to now systematically accumulate the two metals. As of November 20, physical gold with 24 karat purity is trading ₹12,557 per gram which is nearly 30% lower than its record high price of ₹ 17885 per gram. The price of physical silver has also slipped to ₹175000 per kilogram, over 57% compared to its record high, achieved earlier this year. Gold futures trading on the Multi Commodity Exchange with December 4, 2026 expiry are also down nearly 30% from the recent high as of November 20. Silver futures with December 4, 2026 expiry are down by over 52% compared to their recent high.
 How DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds is changing its strategy
 According to DSP Mutual Fund's Signals & Stance note, the scheme has maintained an underweight position in precious metals compared to its underlying benchmark since its inception. Notably, the benchmark index of the scheme is a composite of the Nifty 500 Total Returns Index (TRI) and the Nifty Composite Debt Index along with the domestic prices of gold and silver.
 The mutual fund house added that while peer funds remained neutral or overweight on precious metals, the DSP scheme ran a 50% underweight position on gold and silver. The scheme held roughly 10% in gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and had no exposure to silver ETFs, aside from a brief 50 basis points trade undertaken in June 2026.
 The fund house has announced that it has started executing a ‘rules-based’ buying strategy to change its underweight stance. As opposed to trying to time the market bottom or chase upward momentum, the mutual fund house intends to increase the scheme’s exposure to gold and silver in a staggered manner.
 In order to do so, the fund is deploying capital at predetermined international price levels as sellers dominate. For gold, the fund house has initiated a 50 basis points addition near $3,850 per ounce, with plans to add another 50 basis points for every $100 per ounce drop at $3,800, $3,700, $3,600, and subsequent levels. |
 For silver, it began adding 50 basis points just below $47 per ounce and will add another 50 basis points for every $2 decline. If silver breaches $42 per ounce, the fund will accelerate purchases to 1% alongside a one-time 50 basis points addition, meaning a slide from $47 to $37 would result in a cumulative 5% portfolio allocation.
 Why DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds is changing its strategy
 According to the note, the change in strategy is anchored in DSP's five-point valuation and macroeconomic framework for precious metals. The fund house mentioned in the note that valuations have moved into an attractive territory as gold is trading at roughly a 15% discount to fair value, while silver sits at a steep 28% discount.
 The fund also tracks incremental demand from central banks, ETFs, and jewellery buyers. According to the note, while central bank buying remains steady, jewellery demand has been muted, but the fund house expects a time and price correction to revive physical jewellery consumption.
 The fund house also mentioned that it expects a strengthening US Dollar Index to act as a short-term headwind which could trigger deeper price drops, providing the entry points the fund wants.
 The fund house also cited the Gold-Silver Ratio climbing past 82. Notably, this is above its 21st-century average of 69. This development signals relative undervaluation in silver. Additionally, DSP Mutual Fund also sees oversold readings and low speculative participation in futures and ETFs as a sign of rapid selling creating favorable risk-reward conditions.
 Portfolio adjustments ahead
 As DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds builds its gold and silver holdings back toward a neutral or overweight position from its underweight stance, it plans to fund these purchases through a reduction in its debt allocation and by trimming exposure to select equity sectors.
